name: SN74LVC8T245PWR
title: SN74LVC8T245: 8-bit dual-supply bus transceiver, 1.65 V to 5.5 V on each port, 3-state outputs
summary: An eight-channel non-inverting bus transceiver for moving logic signals between two supply domains. Port A and the DIR and OE controls run from VCCA, port B from VCCB, and each supply may be set anywhere from 1.65 V to 5.5 V. DIR picks the direction for all eight channels and an active-low OE turns both ports' outputs off. Outputs go high-impedance when either supply is below 100 mV or floating, the part supports partial power-down through Ioff, and the supplies may come up in any order. Packages are SOIC (DW), SOP (NS), SSOP (DB, DBQ), TSSOP (PW), TVSOP (DGV) and VQFN (RHL), all 24 pins, rated -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 8, direction set by DIR, outputs gated by OE

circuits.title: 1.8 V controller to 5 V system, eight lines
circuits.description: Eight data lines go up from a controller on 1.8 V to a system on 5 V. VCCA is on the 1.8 V rail with a 0.1 µF capacitor; VCCB is on the 5 V rail with 0.1 µF and 1 µF. DIR is pulled up to 1.8 V, fixing the direction A to B. OE is driven by the controller and also pulled up to 1.8 V. The controller drives A1 to A8 and B1 to B8 drive the system's data inputs. All three blocks share one ground.

circuits.title: Load circuit for switching measurements
circuits.description: The output under test sees CL and one RL to ground, and a second RL to the common of switch S1. S1 is left open for propagation delays, set to 2 × VCCO for tPLZ and tPZL, and set to ground for tPHZ and tPZH. CL is 15 pF and each RL is 2 kΩ at every VCCO.

operation.text: Eight non-inverting transceivers between bus A and bus B. With OE low, DIR high turns on the B outputs and A data appears on B; DIR low turns on the A outputs and B data appears on A. OE high turns both ports' outputs off (isolation). One DIR and one OE serve all eight channels.

VCCA powers port A and VCCB powers port B; each may be anywhere from 1.65 V to 5.5 V, independently, so the part translates between any of the 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V levels in either direction. DIR and OE are powered from VCCA and their thresholds follow it.
The input stages of both ports stay active whatever DIR and OE are set to, so every A and B pin needs a valid HIGH or LOW level; a floating input draws excess ICC and ICCZ.
Unused I/Os are tied to GND, and no I/O is left floating while the direction is changed.

When either supply is under 100 mV or disconnected while the other is within its operating range, both ports are first pulled down weakly and then their outputs are disabled to high impedance, with the supply current held. The I/Os should not be driven, or should be held low, before a supply is disconnected. Ioff sets the most current that can leak into or out of a pin.

The Ioff circuit turns the outputs off when the device is unpowered, so the pins go high-impedance and no damaging current flows back into the part. The part is fully specified for partial-power-down use through Ioff.

Ground goes to the GND pins first. After that the two supplies may come up or go down in either order with no glitch on the I/Os, so a downstream device does not see a false bit, reset or configuration.

To keep the outputs off while supplies ramp, OE is tied to VCC through a pull-up resistor; the smallest usable resistor is set by how much current the circuit driving OE can sink. OE is kept high until VCCA and VCCB are both up.

Push-pull CMOS outputs that sink and source about equal currents. With a light load the strong drive gives very fast edges, which can ring unless the routing and the load are considered. The outputs can deliver more current than the part survives; the absolute maximum limits apply at all times. Two outputs may be tied together for twice the drive. At a 5 V supply the output current is up to 32 mA.

The input voltage range comes from the supply of the device driving the transceiver: a HIGH must be above the input port's VIH and a LOW below its VIL. The output voltage range comes from the supply of the device being driven.

Each supply has a bypass capacitor; traces are short to limit loading. Pads on the signal lines for load capacitors or pull-up resistors let the rise and fall times be tuned to the system. A bypass capacitor sits next to VCCA (pin 1) and another next to VCCB (pins 23, 24), with vias to an inner ground plane.
ESD protection beyond JESD 22: 4000 V human-body model (A114-A) and 1000 V charged-device model (C101). Latch-up performance passes 100 mA per JESD 78, class II.
An automotive version, SN74LVC8T245-Q1, and an enhanced-product version, SN74LVC8T245-EP, also exist.
A 2.5 MHz square wave at 1.8 V on the A side comes out as a 5 V square wave on the B side (time base 200 ns/div).
